payload.prompt: Erstellen Sie eine benutzerdefinierte Buchhaltungsdimension "Region" mit den Werten "Vestlandet" und "Midt-Norge". Buchen Sie dann einen Beleg auf Konto 6540 über 8600 NOK, verknüpft mit dem Dimensionswert "Vestlandet".

payload.goal: Create a custom accounting dimension 'Region' with values 'Vestlandet' and 'Midt-Norge', then post a voucher to account 6540 for 8600 NOK linked to dimension value 'Vestlandet'.
success_checks: Custom dimension 'Region' is created and visible in Tripletex
Voucher is posted to account 6540 with amount 8600 NOK
Voucher entry is linked to dimension value 'Vestlandet'
risk_notes: Custom dimensions may require a specific Tripletex module to be enabled (e.g., 'Dimensjoner' module) — verify module activation first
Account 6540 must exist in the chart of accounts; if not, it must be created or mapped
No counter-account specified for the voucher — a balancing account (e.g., bank or accounts payable) must be determined
VAT treatment for account 6540 (typically a cost account) is not specified — risk_notes: VAT rate unclear, may be 25% or exempt
No voucher date specified — will default to today's date unless otherwise instructed
No description/reference provided for the voucher posting
Sandbox is empty — all prerequisite setup (dimension module, accounts) must be completed before posting
payload.suggested_first_action: Enable the custom dimensions module in Tripletex via POST /module or settings, then create the 'Region' dimension via POST /dimension.

line_items.description: Voucher posting to account 6540 linked to dimension 'Vestlandet'

ordered_steps: 1. Enable custom dimensions module: POST /module {name: 'dimensjon'} or verify it is active in company settings
2. Create custom dimension 'Region': POST /dimension {name: 'Region', isActive: true}
5. Verify account 6540 exists: GET /ledger/account?number=6540; create if missing
6. Determine balancing/counter account (e.g., bank account or creditor account) for the voucher
7. Post voucher: POST /ledger/voucher with postings: [{account: 6540, amount: 8600, dimensionValue: <vestlandetId>}, {account: <counterAccount>, amount: -8600}]
8. Verify voucher is balanced and dimension link is confirmed: GET /ledger/voucher/{id}

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Add new voucher. IMPORTANT: Also creates postings. Only the gross amounts will be used. Amounts should be rounded to 2 decimals.
Create a new free (aka 'user defined') accounting dimension
Create a new value for one of the free (aka 'user defined') accounting dimensions

rules: ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.

When using vatType != 0 (e.g. VAT 25%), include ONLY the debit posting with the GROSS amount (incl VAT). Tripletex auto-generates VAT split and credit posting. If this fails with a balance error, fall back to manual postings for all legs.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
For salary/payroll vouchers, set employee={"id": employee_id} on each posting.
Always resolve account numbers via GET /ledger/account?number=XXXX first, then use account={"id": resolved_id}.
Postings with vatType={"id":0} (exempt) can include both debit and credit lines manually.

payload.text:
Let me analyze the task:

1. Create a custom accounting dimension "Region" with values "Vestlandet" and "Midt-Norge"
2. Post a voucher to account 6540 for 8600 NOK linked to dimension value "Vestlandet"

Following the trace template:
1. GET /ledger/account?number=6540 - resolve expense account
2. GET /ledger/account?number=1920 - resolve counter-account (bank)
3. POST /ledger/accountingDimensionName - create "Region" dimension
4. POST /ledger/accountingDimensionValue - create "Vestlandet" value


5. POST /ledger/accountingDimensionValue - create "Midt-Norge" value
6. POST /ledger/voucher - create the voucher

I can run steps 1-3 in parallel since the account lookups and dimension creation are independent. The dimension name will get an auto-assigned `dimensionIndex`, which I'll then use when creating the dimension values. Finally, I'll post the voucher with the dimension reference attached to the appropriate line.

Let me start by resolving the accounts and setting up the dimension name concurrently.
I'll analyze the task and execute it following the trace template. Let me start by resolving accounts and creating the dimension in parallel.

payload.headline: Perfect run: all 6 checks passed with only 6 API calls and zero errors.
what_worked: Parallel account lookups and dimension creation minimized round-trips, achieving a clean 6-call run.
Correct use of freeAccountingDimension1 with dimensionIndex=1 linked the voucher posting to 'Vestlandet' properly.
what_to_try_next: Consider caching known account IDs (e.g., 1920 bank account) across tasks to skip redundant GET /ledger/account lookups.

If dimensionIndex is always auto-assigned sequentially, the GET response from POST /ledger/accountingDimensionName already provides it — no extra lookup needed, which is already being done correctly here.
Explore whether both dimension values can be batch-created in a single POST to further reduce call count if the API supports arrays.
